description: upload-media-types (ADR 0031, ADR 0013): the media types an upload is admitted under, said once for both tiers. The app's bind act refuses a type outside `admitted` with `media-type-refused`, before a byte is read and while the Admin still has the file (packages/core/src/sources/binding.ts, `UPLOAD_MEDIA_TYPES`); the worker's converter dispatches on the media type the catalogue row carries, one converter per type, and quarantines a document whose type has none under `UnsupportedMediaType` (apps/worker/src/better_answers_worker/pipeline/converter.py, `CONVERTERS`). The two lists are one answer held by two tiers: a type the app admits and the worker cannot convert is a binding that will never answer anything, and a type the worker converts and the app refuses is a converter nothing reaches. `admitted` is a set — its order means nothing and each tier compares it sorted. `outside` is not the complement, which is unbounded; it is a few types chosen because each is the nearest way one tier would drift from the other, and each tier's seeded suite offers the same ones: the app's sees them refused at the bind act (packages/core/test/sources.test.ts), the worker's sees them quarantined on the catalogue row rather than converted (apps/worker/tests/test_pipeline_index.py). Admitting a new media type is a change to this file and to both tiers in one commit, which moves the contract's digest with it, and under ADR 0013 it is also the choice of that type's one converter. Neither tier imports the other's constant, and neither suite writes the list out itself.

outside.why: Word's older format, the nearest neighbour of an admitted type and the likeliest fifth: no converter was chosen for it (ADR 0013), so neither tier takes it on the strength of `.docx`

text, and still outside: the two passed-through types are named, never matched by a `text/` prefix. HTML is no upload type — the website connector names its converter at S4 under ADR 0013's one-converter rule — so until then neither tier takes it
